evals.name: vague-prompt-asks-before-rewriting
evals.prompt: Improve this prompt for Claude Code: "fix the login bug"
evals.expected_output: Should fetch all three guidance pages (best-practices, model-config, sub-agents), name the request's shape as a BUG in one line, then recognize the prompt is missing symptom, likely location, and definition of fixed. Should ask about ALL THREE of those missing pieces — what users observe, where auth lives, and how to verify the fix — one at a time, offering multiple choice where the options are knowable, and should NOT rewrite the parts that are already clear while anything is still unclear. Should NOT attempt to fix any bug itself and should NOT invent requirements.

evals.name: clear-prompt-one-shot-rewrite
evals.prompt: Rewrite my prompt: "add tests for src/utils/date.ts — we use Vitest, I care about DST edge cases, done means npm test passes, don't touch the implementation"
evals.expected_output: Should fetch all three guidance pages (best-practices, model-config, sub-agents), name the shape as a ONE-SHOT TASK in one line, then rewrite in ONE shot (no clarifying questions — scope, verification, and non-goals are all present). Output, in order: the rewritten prompt in a fenced code block (scoped task, verification command with a demand for evidence, explicit do-not-touch); one line naming the guidance used (each live URL plus the fetch date); a bulleted what-changed-and-why list tied to best-practice rules; and an offer to run it now or paste into a fresh session. Must NOT assign models to anything: the rewrite dispatches no subagents, so the model-assignment step is skipped.

evals.name: fetch-failure-uses-fallback
evals.prompt: (WebFetch is unavailable in this environment.) Make this prompt better: "refactor the payment service, it's getting messy"
evals.expected_output: Should attempt the live fetches, fail, then fall back to the bundled reference for EACH page that failed (references/best-practices-checklist.md for the best-practices page, references/model-selection.md for model-config and sub-agents) — the fallback is per-source, not conditional on whether model assignment ends up applying and explicitly warn the user the guidance may be stale. The staleness warning must also appear in the deliverable as the line naming which guidance was used — naming the fallback file(s), not the live URLs. Should still proceed: the prompt is ambiguous (which files, what does better look like, what must not break), so it asks before rewriting rather than guessing.

evals.name: large-feature-emits-interview-kickoff-prompt
evals.prompt: Improve this prompt: "build a multi-tenant billing system with usage metering, proration, and a self-serve plan switcher"
evals.expected_output: Should name the request's shape as a LARGE FEATURE and say so. The deliverable must STILL BE A PROMPT — the interview kickoff prompt from the guidance, adapted to this billing feature, instructing Claude to interview the user with AskUserQuestion and write a complete spec to SPEC.md — plus the instruction to execute that spec in a fresh session. Should NOT decline the job, and should NOT hand back a workflow recommendation or a plan in place of a prompt. The model-assignment step must NOT fire: an interview kickoff prompt dispatches nothing, so the delivered prompt must name no model and no effort level.

evals.name: negative-trigger-llm-app-system-prompt
evals.prompt: Help me write a good system prompt for my customer-support chatbot built on the Claude API
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill — the request is prompt engineering for the user's own LLM application, not a prompt aimed at Claude Code. The Claude API / claude-api guidance applies instead.

evals.name: negative-control-baseline-without-skill
evals.prompt: (BASELINE ARM — run this with the prompt-creator skill NOT loaded. Deliberately the same rough prompt as case 1.) Improve this prompt for Claude Code: "fix the login bug"
evals.expected_output: This case has no pass/fail of its own; it exists so case 1 can be read as evidence rather than assumed. Record what the model does unaided. A pass for the skill is a visible DELTA against this baseline, not merely a good-looking answer: without the skill, expect no live fetch of the best-practices page, no named request shape, no line naming which guidance was used, and a plausible chance the model simply starts diagnosing the login bug instead of rewriting the prompt. If the baseline already matches case 1, the skill is not causing the behavior and its wording needs work — that is the finding. Where the runner supports it, `claude plugin eval --ablation with-without` produces this arm automatically and should be preferred over reading this case by hand.

evals.name: fan-out-prompt-assigns-a-model-per-agent
evals.prompt: Improve this prompt: "use subagents to check all 40 packages under packages/ for unused dependencies, then have another agent write up the findings in a report"
evals.expected_output: Should fetch all three guidance pages and, because the rewritten prompt dispatches subagents, must run the model-assignment step. The delivered prompt must name a model PER AGENT — not one model for the whole fan-out — with one clause of justification each: a cheap tier (e.g. haiku) for the 40 mechanical per-package dependency scans because they need breadth without judgment, and a higher tier (e.g. opus, optionally with an effort level) for the synthesis/report agent because it weighs everything the scans return. The what-changed-and-why list must include the model assignments and should name silent inheritance — that unassigned agents would all have run on the main session's model — as the defect being fixed. Should justify from the alias descriptions and the cost-versus-judgment axis, and must NOT invent benchmarks or measured cost/accuracy claims.

evals.name: negative-single-agent-prompt-gets-no-model-line
evals.prompt: Rewrite my prompt: "add a --dry-run flag to scripts/deploy.sh — done means ./scripts/deploy.sh --dry-run prints the plan and exits 0, and the real deploy path must not change"
evals.expected_output: Should name the shape as a ONE-SHOT TASK and rewrite in one shot (scope, verification, and a non-goal are all present). The model-assignment step must NOT fire: the rewrite dispatches no subagents, parallel agents, or workflow, so the delivered prompt must contain NO model assignment, no model alias, and no effort level, and the what-changed-and-why list must not mention model choice. Naming a model here is a FAILURE even if the choice would be sensible — it is the noise the step's precondition exists to prevent. Still expected: the fenced rewritten prompt, the guidance line with each live URL and fetch date, the what-changed-and-why list, and the offer to run it now or in a fresh session.
